ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a shaded triangle on the right. Its bottom side is horizontal and labeled 30 mm. Its left side is vertical, so it can serve as the height to that horizontal base. On the left of the shaded triangle there is an auxiliary dashed right triangle: the dashed slanted side is labeled 20 mm, the horizontal leg is labeled 12 mm, and a right-angle mark shows it is a right triangle. Reasoning: The vertical side of the shaded triangle is the same height as the vertical leg of the auxiliary dashed right triangle. In the dashed right triangle, the hypotenuse is 20 mm and one leg is 12 mm, so by the Pythagorean theorem the height is h = sqrt(20^2 - 12^2) = sqrt(400 - 144) = sqrt(256) = 16 mm. The area of the shaded triangle is A = 1/2 * base * height = 1/2 * 30 * 16 = 240.

method.method_draft: Read the shaded triangle from the image: its horizontal base is labeled 30 mm, and its left side is vertical, so that side is the height to the base. Also read the auxiliary dashed right triangle on the left: the dashed slanted segment from the top vertex is 20 mm, and the horizontal leg from the dashed foot to the vertical side is 12 mm. Use the Pythagorean theorem on this auxiliary right triangle to find the vertical height: h = sqrt(20^2 - 12^2) = 16 mm. Then use the triangle area formula A = 1/2 bh with b = 30 and h = 16, giving A = 240.
